source_text: Egi certe, ut fidem disputationis decebat; illudque quod tu argumentando effeceras, id est, ideo in opere Dei ortam voluntatem malam quia fuisset homo creatus ex nihilo, ratio perscrutata contrivit; ostendens videlicet, te immutatis vocabulis idem dixisse, quod Manichaeus finxit et credidit, id est, primum quoque peccatum aeternarum tenebrarum violentia genitum.
pass_a_gloss: I treated certainly as the faith of disputation became; and that which you had effected by arguing, that is, that therefore an evil will arose in a work of God because the human had been created from nothing, a searched reason crushed; showing namely that you with unchanged words said the same which Manichaeus feigned and believed, that is, that the first sin also was generated by the violence of eternal darkness.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: I have certainly proceeded as the honesty of debate required. Careful investigation by reason has crushed what your argument established: that the evil will arose in God’s work because the human being had been created from nothing. It has shown that, with changed terms, you said the same thing Mani invented and believed: that the first sin too was generated by the violence of eternal darkness.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
